title: Quantifying Thiamin Cellular Quotas in Algae
author: Magdalena Gutowska
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.j6ncrde

steps.title: Maintain Algal Cultures
steps.instruction: Maintain CCMP2090 Emiliania huxleyi cultures in mid-exponential growth for ≥10 generations using semi-continuous batch culture techniques in artificial seawater based medium L1-Si.

substeps.instruction: Regularly check axenicity using DAPI DNA stain and epifluorescence microscopy.
Use dedicated media bottles for each thiamin concentration to avoid carry-over.

steps.title: Manage Cell Density and Growth
steps.instruction: Transfer cells to maintain a concentration not exceeding 1 x 10^6 cells mL-1, quantifying concentrations via flow cytometer (e.g., Accuri C6).

substeps.instruction: Transfer daily for replete vitamin amendment conditions.
Transfer every second day for limited vitamin amendment conditions.

steps.title: Set Up Vitamin Treatments
steps.instruction: Establish triplicate cultures for each of the following three vitamin amendment conditions and maintain in mid-exponential growth for ≥10 generations:

substeps.instruction: Luxury treatment: supply thiamin at 300 nmol L-1.
Replete conditions: supply thiamin and HMP at 10 nmol L-1.
Limiting conditions: supply thiamin at 500 pmol L-1 and HMP at 100 pmol L-1.

steps.title: Wash and Concentrate Cells
steps.instruction: Remove vitamin amendments from media using centrifugation washes. Work on ice with a centrifuge pre-cooled to 4°C and resuspend cells gently between steps.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge 100 mL of culture at 4000 x g for 10 min at 4°C.
Remove supernatant, add 50 mL of thiamin-free medium, and repeat the wash/centrifugation process three times.
Resuspend the final pellet in 1.5 mL of thiamin-free medium and quantify cell concentration on a flow cytometer.

steps.title: Generate Final Cell Pellet
steps.instruction: Isolate the final cell pellet and determine the exact cell count.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at 10,000 x g for 30 min at 4°C.
Collect and retain the supernatant in a separate tube.
Flash-freeze the pellet in liquid nitrogen and store at -80°C.
Quantify cell concentration in the combined supernatant aliquots via flow cytometer.
Subtract the supernatant cell count from the total cell numbers determined prior to final centrifugation to find the final pellet cell count.
Monitor chlorophyll fluorescence and FALS distribution on flow cytometer histograms to ensure cells remained intact (<1% ruptured).

steps.title: Extract Pellets for Thiochrome Assay
steps.instruction: Perform pellet extraction to oxidize thiamin to thiochrome under basic conditions.

substeps.instruction: Suspend pellet in 100 μL of 7% HClO4 and sonicate for 2 min.
Add 50 μL 4 M CH3CO2K and 50 μL 30 mg mL-1 K3[Fe(CN)6] in 7 M NaOH.
Pipette to mix and leave for 1 min.
Immediately neutralize the reaction with 6 M aqueous HCl.
Centrifuge the sample and collect the supernatant for analysis.

steps.title: Configure Reverse Phase HPLC
steps.instruction: Set up the HPLC system for thiamin quantification.

substeps.instruction: Purify deionized water for reagents using active charcoal and filtration.
Use an Agilent 1200 series reverse phase HPLC with fluorescence detection (excitation 365 nm, emission 444 nm).
Equip with a Supelcosil SPLC-18-DB column (25 cm x 10 mm, 5 μm).
Set the gradient using A) H2O, B) K2HPO4 (pH 6.6), and C) CH3OH as follows: 0-5 min 100% B; 14 min 7% A/70% B/23% C; 25 min 25% A/75% C; 28-34 min 100% B.

steps.title: Quantify Thiamin Quotas
steps.instruction: Determine the concentrations of thiamin species in the samples.

substeps.instruction: Construct a calibration curve using known concentrations of thiamin pyrophosphate (TPP), thiamin monophosphate (TMP), and free thiamin (ThF).
Integrate the fluorescence signal peak areas.
Plot the fluorescence signal peak area of the samples against the standard curves to quantify ThF, TMP, and TPP.
